title: Wildcards: * and ?
summary: How one short pattern becomes a list of file names, before the command even starts.

scheme: rm receives:  rm a.tmp b.tmp old.tmp
text: * means "any characters, or none". The shell replaces the pattern with the matching names, then runs the command.
- rm never sees the *: it only gets the list.

scheme: [abc]*     names starting with a, b or c
text: - [ ] is one character from the list.
- Names starting with a dot (hidden files) are left out by *.
Not sure what a pattern will match? echo it first: you see the list, nothing is deleted.
- Quotes stop the expansion: '*.tmp' stays plain text.
- In bash, if nothing matches, the pattern is left as it is: echo *.xyz prints *.xyz (zsh stops instead: next page).
You type in zsh: when no file matches a pattern, zsh stops the line with "no matches found", and the command doesn't run at all. bash would run it with the pattern as it is.
- Either way, look with ls before you rm.
